recipes.name: M's Sloppy Joe Sauce
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup barbeque sauce (such as KC Masterpiece®)

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add onion and bell pepper; cook until beginning to soften, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and ground turkey; cook and stir until turkey is completely crumbled and browned, another 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir in puréed tomatoes, barbecue sauce, ketchup, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, and chile-garlic sauce. Simmer until completely heated, 7 to 10 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: M's Sloppy Joe Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This Sloppy Joe recipe is a bit more flavorful and spicy than than what you're probably used to, thanks to barbecue sauce and a bit of Sriracha.

review.reviewBody: My family loved this! I had to make some substitutions because we didn't have everything. I was out of vinegar so I used lemon juice and didn't have any chile garlic sauce so I used hot chili powder and extra garlic. My mom found it too hot but my two year old gobbled it up and my husband and I added hot sauce to ours so be careful. It was a great quick family dinner, Thanks

A good recipe but....
I simply had to play with it to amp up the flavor and dial up the healthy:
1. Omitted the pureed tomatoes and used a can of tomato paste for texture and richness.
2. Used balsamic vinegar instead of white vinegar which added a savory layer.
3 Omitted the processed ketchup and used a 1/2 TBS of brown sugar for the "sweet".
4. Added finely chopped mushrooms to the almost cooked ground turkey to "beef" up the meat and add fiber and vitamin D to my meal.
Finally, I did not add any salt. The flavor changes enhanced this dish enough so that I did not need to add any extra sodium. This was delicious on the leftover wheat pita pocket bread I had from a previous meal (lower calories than a bun!)

I think the last time I made sloppy joes was over 30 years ago with my mom, using the canned sauce. Out of the blue I got a craving for them and tried this recipe. I loved it! I don't typically buy BBQ sauce but I bake a lot and always have molasses on hand, so I substituted 4 tablespoons of molasses, 1 teaspoon of garlic powder, a teaspoon of cayenne, and a tablespoon of tomato paste in its place and it turned out fabulous! I also did a vegan version, using ground portobello mushrooms in place of ground turkey or beef.

Mmmm, spicy. Sloppy Joes with a kick, so this may not be suitable for those who can't tolerate a little heat. This wasn't spicy hot by any means, but it was medium spicy. I used ground beef and a cup of frozen fajita vegetables (onions, green red yellow and orange bell peppers) and added 1/2 tsp of onion powder since I didn't have any other onion. I diced them up. I subbed a can of roma tomato paste and two cans of water for the puree. BBQ sauce used was Sweet Baby Rays Original and chili paste in the jar but it still had the same rooster picture as the liquid sauce. I added a little salt as the beef was browning and simmered this until the sauce thickened about 25 minutes, This was very good and I would definitely make this again but it isn't quite your traditional sloppy joes. Very very good though. Thanks!

Absolutely mouth watering! Made a few substitutions only because it was what I had on hand: Ground chicken instead of turkey, tomato paste instead of purée/ hot sauce instead of surakarta, & omitted the green peppers but didn’t miss them because the flavor was incredible! I usually hate it when people rave about a recipe they‘ve completely recreated but the changes I made were so subtle they didn’t disrupt the spirit of this recipe - sweet, tangy, & a touch of spice. This is now a family favorite!

Wow what a delicious meal!!! M's Sloppy Joe Sauce pushes the others to the side. The sauce remains saucy so it is more sloppy than the others but not messy. I ate these as an open faced sandwich (knife and fork) as well as on a bun and I didn't wear any of the filling, ever. The sauce is tangy, not too sweet. I made my own bbq sauce and had to use Angostura bitters instead of Worcestershire sauce for health reasons. The outcome was a flavourful, savoury with a hint of sweet, thick sauce that melts in your mouth. The key here is the garlic chili sauce. It has that pungent aroma and kick when you taste it but never too spicy and not too overpowering. It simply coheres with the other flavors. This is not the school cafetteria version, this is adult sloppy joes. Sip a cold beer with these and you'll be happy you finally grew up! Thanks Semigourmet for sharing your wonderful recipe.
I loved the garlic and spiciness of this sauce, however it was way too sour for my taste. I added two tbsp. of brown sugar plus a dash of liquid smoke. Yummy!

This was my first attempt at homemade sloppy joes and it turned out great! I couldn't find the chile-garlic sauce, so I used a teaspoon of minced garlic and a can of green chiles. It was a saucy-sweetness that my husband loved.
It's a great recipe for turkey sloppy joe. I used a whole can of crushed tomatoes, red sweet peppers and used Bachan's Japanese bbq sauce. It doesn't have smoke flavor. Excellent!

Yum. I made this with minor changes using what I had on hand. So, Dijon mustard instead of brown. Cider vinegar instead of white. I used a can of diced petite tomatoes and pureed that with the other sauce ingredients and added one extra clove of garlic to the mix. This was an easy, adaptable all purpose recipe. Good stuff.

My new fave sloppy joe recipe! Finally, a sloppy joe recipe worthy of adult tastes. I made these with just a couple small tweaks, tomato sauce instead of puree and skipped the ketchup, and used ground turkey. LOVE the addition of Sriracha sauce, how clever! Adds a great spice and a touch of heat. Wonderful recipe, and a do-over for sure. Thanks for this terrific submission, Semigourmet.
Turned out really good, I used homemade tomato paste so it turned out a little bit thinner than I wanted. But so good! Family approved!

Did anyone actually try this recipe, as is, without a complete makeover? I did and it was great. How can you comment on this recipe when it is not the same? Instead of reviews, it should be, “ Your Changes” .
The easiest, most flavorful sloppy Joe sauce! That's a keeper! Thanks for the share!
This was really delicious! The only change I made was Dijon only because I didn’t have brown mustard. Served on a brioche bun from Aldi..so good, and super quick.

Now more than ever I am trying to find new “dinner recipes.” I had a hankering for sloppy Joe’s but wanted to use ground turkey. Normally I flipped through see what people use and do my own. This one was so specific I decided to follow it exactly. It was delicious. I am making it for the second time this week.
Not spectacular but good as is.

I made this instead of buying the canned sauce. My family couldn't even tell the difference! I ran out of ketchup and used a couple tablespoons of brown sugar. I'll probably use a little more ground meat (all I had was 1.30 pounds) so the sauce isn't dripping on the plate. Very good recipe. I'll make this again.
I made this for 20 servings. It was a big hit. This is a sloppy joe recipe I will use over and over again. No more sloppy joe mix packets from the store.
Loved the tang and little bit of spice! This is my new go to sloppy joe sauce :)
